content.user_title: Build Azure Event Hubs Python Streams
content.value_statement: Python teams need reliable Event Hubs examples for producers, consumers, and checkpointing. This skill provides focused Azure SDK patterns for streaming ingestion and processing.
actual_capabilities: Shows installation commands for azure-eventhub, azure-identity, and blob checkpoint packages.
Demonstrates producer and consumer clients with DefaultAzureCredential.
Explains event batching, partition IDs, and partition keys.
Shows consumer callbacks with checkpoint updates and BlobCheckpointStore.
Covers async producer and consumer patterns for higher throughput.
Includes event property inspection and Event Hub partition metadata examples.
limitations: Provides documentation examples only, not a complete runnable project.
Uses placeholder namespaces, Event Hub names, storage accounts, and containers.
Does not provision Azure infrastructure, assign RBAC roles, or configure networking.
Requires validation against the installed Azure SDK versions and target environment.

use_cases.title: Create streaming ingestion
use_cases.description: Build Python producers that batch events and send them to Azure Event Hubs.

use_cases.title: Process events reliably
use_cases.description: Add consumers that update checkpoints after successful event handling.

use_cases.title: Plan production consumers
use_cases.description: Compare checkpointing, partition keys, async clients, and consumer groups before implementation.

prompt_templates.title: Create a producer
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to outline a Python Event Hubs producer. Include packages, authentication, batching, and the values I must provide.

prompt_templates.title: Add a consumer
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design a Python Event Hubs consumer callback. Include starting position, event body handling, and checkpoint timing.

prompt_templates.title: Design checkpointing
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to plan BlobCheckpointStore for my Event Hubs consumer. List required Azure resources, credentials, and failure considerations.

prompt_templates.title: Review a pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to review my Event Hubs Python pipeline for batching, partition keys, async usage, consumer groups, and cleanup.

output_examples.input: I need to send telemetry from Python to Event Hubs.
output_examples.output: A producer plan with package requirements, DefaultAzureCredential setup, batch creation, send timing, and required namespace and Event Hub values.

output_examples.input: I need a reliable consumer for production processing.
output_examples.output: A consumer checklist covering callback responsibilities, checkpoint timing, Blob storage requirements, consumer group choice, and validation steps.

output_examples.input: I want to improve throughput for my Event Hubs app.
output_examples.output: A review of batching, async clients, partition key choices, load balancing, and cleanup practices for high-volume streams.

best_practices: Use managed identity or DefaultAzureCredential with least required permissions.
Checkpoint only after successful processing to avoid losing events.
Use batching, async clients, and partition keys when throughput or ordering matters.
anti_patterns: Do not hardcode production secrets, connection strings, or tenant-specific identifiers in prompts.
Do not checkpoint before the event handler finishes durable work.
Do not reuse the default consumer group for unrelated applications.

faq.question: Does this skill provision Azure resources?
faq.answer: No. It explains Python SDK usage and assumes Azure resources already exist.

faq.question: Can it help with managed identity authentication?
faq.answer: Yes. The examples use DefaultAzureCredential, which supports managed identity and local developer credentials.

faq.question: Does it cover checkpointing?
faq.answer: Yes. It shows checkpoint updates and BlobCheckpointStore setup for production consumers.

faq.question: Can it design async consumers?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes async producer and consumer patterns for higher throughput scenarios.

faq.question: Does it include monitoring guidance?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on SDK usage, event flow, checkpointing, and partition metadata.

faq.question: What inputs should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide the namespace, Event Hub name, consumer group, storage account URL, container name, and authentication method.
